$comment: Single source of truth for every number, version, licence, and identifier
that OpenEtruscan asserts publicly. Surfaces (README, CITATION.cff,
codemeta.json, SECURITY.md, model cards, the website, PyPI) restate these
values; `scripts/ops/check_release_truth.py` fails CI when a surface drifts.
Edit this file first, then the surfaces. Never the other way round.
An external audit (2026-08-08) found four different version numbers across
four public surfaces and three corpus totals with no machine-readable
reconciliation. This file exists so that cannot recur silently.

canonical_urls.$comment: Every URL a citation or machine-readable record may point at. A path not listed here must not appear in CITATION.cff, codemeta.json, or a model card. `/data` was cited by both and has never existed — it 404s.

corpus_counts.$comment: Three totals, three different artifacts. They are not in conflict; they were merely never reconciled in one machine-readable place. Any public statement of a corpus size must name which of these it means.

archival.label: unified platform corpus
archival.what: Every record in the platform database after unification of the Larth Dataset (~71%) and CIE Vol. I extractions (~29%).

published.label: cleaned ML-ready corpus
published.what: The Zenodo deposit. 66 rows dropped from the archival corpus during cleaning.

deployed.label: live production database
deployed.what: Every row in the `inscriptions` table of the production database. This is also exactly what the Pelagios JSON-LD and VoID endpoints serve: `getPelagiosFeedRows()` is an unfiltered `SELECT ... FROM inscriptions` and `getVoidStats()` is `COUNT(*)`, so the feed's `total` is the table count, not a subset.
deployed.open_item: Earlier wording here blamed an undocumented feed filter. That was wrong: there is no filter. The live database simply holds 701 fewer rows than the archival corpus and 635 fewer than the published Zenodo deposit — the deployed platform serves a smaller corpus than the one its DOI cites. The cause is unknown from the application code alone (candidates: prod seeded from an older or partial export; rows lost in the Cloud SQL -> Neon migration; cleaning applied at load). Resolving it needs database and pipeline access. Owner: Pod A. Until resolved, no surface may present 6,633 or 6,567 as the size of what the website serves.
deployed.downstream_staleness: README's provenance table (acquired_documented 2,317 / acquired_undocumented 4,316, summing to 6,633) describes the archival corpus. The live API reports 2,203 / 3,729. Both are internally consistent; they describe different artifacts and must be labelled as such.

licences.$comment: Per artifact, not per repository. Inbound and outbound differ for data and that is deliberate: contributions are accepted CC0 so the aggregate can be redistributed under a single outbound licence without per-contributor negotiation.

code.applies_to: everything in src/, scripts/, services/, tests/, and the frontend repository

data_outbound.applies_to: the Zenodo deposit, the LOD feeds, and every corpus export
data_outbound.note: Upstream: Larth Dataset CC-BY-4.0; CIE Vol. I public domain (Pauli et al., 1893–).

data_inbound.applies_to: inscription data contributed through PRs, CSV import, or the CLI
data_inbound.note: CC0 in, CC BY 4.0 out. Contributors waive rights so the aggregate carries one outbound licence; the CC-BY attribution obligation downstream runs to the project and its upstream sources, not to individual contributors.

model_weights.applies_to: etr-lora-v4 and every published adapter or checkpoint
model_weights.note: Matches the base-model licence chain (XLM-R / LaBSE).

models.note: The LoRA adapter itself is unevaluated. The only numbers on the card are the LaBSE baseline column of rosetta-eval-v1 and are labelled as such. Rosetta is a documented negative result: best strict precision@10 = 0.0625 on a 22-pair test split, 16 queries actually evaluated. It does not support translation or decipherment claims.

headline_metric.name: macro_f1
headline_metric.eval_set: v2.0.2 candidate-gold, n=143, 3-rater LLM-jury unanimous, Krippendorff alpha 0.7649

retracted_claim.why: In-training-set fit on a self-labelled subset, not held-out performance.
retracted_claim.hub_state_verified: 2026-08-08. README.md states 'Achieves **99% Macro F1**'. Also wrong on the same card: language code `xue` (Etruscan is `ett`), a v0.5.0 title, and a Cloud Run deployment description the project has migrated away from.
hub_machine_readable_residue: metrics.json reports val_f1_macro 0.7427 for the CNN over a 1,497/375 split whose class balance (commercial support 102) contradicts the v2.0.2 finding that commercial is data-starved. Not a corrected figure; not comparable. Retained for provenance, explained in the card.

v2/metadata.json carries baseline_milestone '8,091_verified' — a corpus number matching no OpenEtruscan artifact (6,633 archival / 6,567 published / 5,932 deployed). Stray figure from the retracted era.
retracted_claim.action: Corrected card authored at models/openetruscan-classifier/README.md and gated by check_release_truth.py. Push it with `python scripts/ops/push_model_card.py openetruscan-classifier --push` (requires HF_TOKEN; publishes to a public repo, so it is opt-in rather than a CI step). Flip retracted_on_hub to true and this surface's status to resolved once the push is verified.

supported_versions.$comment: Mirrored by SECURITY.md. Security support tracks shipped minors, not the long-abandoned 0.3.x series.

surfaces.$comment: What restates this manifest. `checked` surfaces are enforced by scripts/ops/check_release_truth.py in CI. `manual` surfaces live outside this repository and are the maintainer's release-checklist responsibility — the checker cannot reach them.

manual.action: Publish the current package. Until then the CITATION and codemeta versions describe software no one can install.
Frontend reads version from its own package.json; podc/s1 aligns all three to this manifest.
See models[].retracted_claim.action. Highest-severity open item in the project.
